claims.statement: Daikin's Stand By Me portal lets owners and installers manage registration, maintenance records, service comments, and warranty-related documents.
Demand hypothesis: multi-brand service networks will pay for a neutral ledger because EU F-gas controls include leak checks and company recordkeeping.

contrary_evidence: Major OEMs already maintain brand-specific service portals.
Not every heat pump or refrigerant charge triggers the same inspection duties.

economics.acquisition_route: One distributor pilot can recruit an existing installer base without founder-led mass selling.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 25000 managed assets across several distributors can produce 3-5 million PLN recurring revenue and founder equity above 5 million PLN in five years.
economics.founder_time: Three to four hours daily for product and channel support.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 82-90% margin once service templates and exports are automated.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 150 technicians and 3000 assets repay initial capital within twelve months.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 80-180 PLN per technician monthly plus 3-8 PLN per managed asset.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Mandatory or warranty-linked service visits renew the evidence record every year.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: The asset-level history and model-specific service rules become harder to replace with every visit.
fingerprint.customer: HVAC service networks, heat-pump installers, and commercial equipment owners.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Refrigerant and HVAC distributors bundle it with technician accounts, parts, or extended-warranty programs.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Mobile capture creates a verified service history and exports audit or warranty-ready dossiers.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A distributor or service network pays per technician and per active asset each month.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A leak check, annual service, or failure requires records that are scattered across technicians, owners, and OEM portals.

founder_fit: Renewable-installation family access supports a low-cost pilot.
Recurring data capture suits analytical automation and limited social energy.
risks: Incorrect compliance prompts could create liability.
Technician data entry may be inconsistent.

structure.commercial_archetype: Recurring compliance ledger with warranty recovery.
structure.control_point: The time-stamped asset service and refrigerant history.
structure.critical_dependency: Reliable technician capture and country-specific rule maintenance.

thesis: A technician-native ledger can preserve maintenance and refrigerant evidence once and reuse it for recurring audits, warranty eligibility, and equipment claims.
title: Heat-Pump Service Evidence Ledger
uncertainties: Distributor willingness to mandate the workflow is unknown.
The addressable multi-brand asset count in Poland is unverified.
